{{Short description|...}}
'''Richard C. Thompson''' [[Order of the British Empire|OBE]] is a [[Marine biology|marine biologist]]. He is Director of the Marine Institute at the [[University of Plymouth]]. Thompson coined the term "[[Microplastics|microplastics]]" in 2004.<ref>{{cite news|first1=Stephen|last1=Buranyi|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=The missing 99%: why can't we find the vast majority of ocean plastic?|url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2019/dec/31/ocean-plastic-we-cant-see|newspaper=The Guardian|date=31 December 2019|issn=0261-3077|via=www.theguardian.com}}</ref>

==Career==
Thompson's paper, "Lost at Sea: Where is All the Plastic?",<ref>https://www.researchgate.net/publication/8575062_Lost_at_Sea_Where_Is_All_the_Plastic</ref> published in the journal ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'' in 2004, was the first to use the term [[microplastics]], which has since become common parlance.<ref>{{cite web|first1=Andrea|last1=Thompson|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Earth Has a Hidden Plastic Problem—Scientists Are Hunting It Down|url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/microplastics-earth-has-a-hidden-plastic-problem-mdash-scientists-are-hunting-it-down/|website=Scientific American}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=To Save the Oceans, Should You Give Up Glitter?|url=https://www.nationalgeographic.com/news/2017/11/glitter-plastics-ocean-pollution-environment-spd/|date=30 November 2017|website=National Geographic News}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Microplastic waste: This massive (tiny) threat to sea life is now in every ocean|url=http://www.independent.co.uk/news/science/microplastic-waste-this-massive-tiny-threat-to-sea-life-is-now-in-every-ocean-9602430.html|date=13 July 2014|website=The Independent}}</ref>

Since 2010 he has been Professor of Marine Biology at the [[University of Plymouth]].<ref name="bio"/> Since 2018 he has also been Director of the Marine Institute, School of Biological and Marine Sciences (Faculty of Science and Engineering) at the University.<ref name="bio">{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Professor Richard Thompson OBE - University of Plymouth|url=https://www.plymouth.ac.uk/staff/richard-thompson|website=www.plymouth.ac.uk}}</ref>

==Awards==
*2016: [[Marsh Award for Marine and Freshwater Conservation]] from the [[Zoological Society of London]] and [[Marsh Christian Trust]]<ref>{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=World leader in microplastic research receives award from the Zoological Society of London|url=https://www.plymouth.ac.uk/news/world-leader-in-microplastic-research-receives-award-from-the-zoological-society-of-london|website=University of Plymouth}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Marsh Christian Trust – Marsh Award for Marine and Freshwater Conservation|url=https://www.marshchristiantrust.org/award/marsh-award-for-marine-and-freshwater-conservation/|website=www.marshchristiantrust.org}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Prestigious awards honour the stars of conservation science|url=https://biaza.org.uk/news/detail/prestigious-awards-honour-the-stars-of-conservation-science|website=[[British and Irish Association of Zoos and Aquariums]]}}</ref>
*2018: [[Order of the British Empire]] (OBE) in the [[2018 New Year Honours]] for services to marine science<ref>{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Professor Richard Thompson made an OBE for services to marine science|url=https://www.plymouth.ac.uk/news/professor-richard-thompson-made-an-obe-for-services-to-marine-science|website=University of Plymouth}}</ref>

==Authored/edited books, chapters and reports== 
*Thompson, R.C., (2006). Plastics. In: Dominant Wave Theory. Hughes, A. and Carson D. pp. 112–116, Booth-Clibborn, London.
*Galgani, F., Fleet, D., van Franeker, J., Katsanevakis, S., Maes, T., Mouat, J.Oosterbaan, L., Poitou, I., Hanke, G., Thompson, R.,  Amato, E., Birkun A., and Janssen, C. (2010) Marine Strategy Framework Directive, TaskGroup 10 Report, Marine Litter. Office for Official Publications of the European Communities, Luxembourg.
*STAP. 2011 Marine Debris as a Global Environmental Problem: Introducing a solutions based framework focused on plastic. In ASTAP Information Document. , pp. 40. Washington, DC: Global Environment Facility. Thompson was lead author.
*GEF. 2012 Secretariat of the Convention on Biological Diversity and Scientific and Technical Advisory Panel GEF,  Impacts of Marine Debris on Biodiversity: Current status and Potential Solutions, vol. 67, pp. 61. Montreal. Thompson was lead author.
*Readman, J.W., DeLuna, F. Ebinhaus, R., Guzman, A.N., Price A.R.G., Readman, E.E. Sheppard, A.L.S., Sleight, A.S. Strum, R. Thompson, R.C. Tonkin, A.Wolschke, H., Wright, R., and Sheppard, R.C. (2013) ''Coral Reefs of the World.''
*Thompson, R.C. (2013) Plastics, Environment and Health. In: Accumulation. ''The Material Politics of Plastics.'' Gabrys, J., Hawkins, G. and Michael, M. pp.150–169.

{{Reflist}}

{{Short description|marine biologist}}
'''Richard C. Thompson''' [[Order of the British Empire|OBE]] is a [[Marine biology|marine biologist]] who researches [[Marine debris|marine litter]]. At the [[University of Plymouth]] he is director of the Marine Institute; professor of Marine Biology; and leads the International Marine Litter Research Unit. Thompson coined the term "[[Microplastics|microplastics]]" in 2004.<ref>{{cite news|first1=Stephen|last1=Buranyi|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=The missing 99%: why can't we find the vast majority of ocean plastic?|url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2019/dec/31/ocean-plastic-we-cant-see|newspaper=The Guardian|date=31 December 2019|issn=0261-3077|via=www.theguardian.com}}</ref>

==Career==
Thompson's paper, "Lost at Sea: Where is All the Plastic?",<ref>https://www.researchgate.net/publication/8575062_Lost_at_Sea_Where_Is_All_the_Plastic</ref> published in the journal ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'' in 2004, was the first to use the term [[microplastics]], which has since become common parlance.<ref>{{cite web|first1=Andrea|last1=Thompson|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Earth Has a Hidden Plastic Problem—Scientists Are Hunting It Down|url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/microplastics-earth-has-a-hidden-plastic-problem-mdash-scientists-are-hunting-it-down/|website=Scientific American}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=To Save the Oceans, Should You Give Up Glitter?|url=https://www.nationalgeographic.com/news/2017/11/glitter-plastics-ocean-pollution-environment-spd/|date=30 November 2017|website=National Geographic News}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Microplastic waste: This massive (tiny) threat to sea life is now in every ocean|url=http://www.independent.co.uk/news/science/microplastic-waste-this-massive-tiny-threat-to-sea-life-is-now-in-every-ocean-9602430.html|date=13 July 2014|website=The Independent}}</ref>

Since 2010 he has been professor of Marine Biology at the [[University of Plymouth]].<ref name="bio"/> Since 2018 he has also been director of the Marine Institute, part of the School of Biological and Marine Sciences at the University.<ref name="bio">{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Professor Richard Thompson OBE - University of Plymouth|url=https://www.plymouth.ac.uk/staff/richard-thompson|website=www.plymouth.ac.uk}}</ref> He also leads the University's International Marine Litter Research Unit.<ref>{{cite web|first1=University of Plymouth Drake Circus Plymouth Devon PL4 8AA United Kingdom +44 1752 600600|last1=Maps|first2=directions Visit us Job|last2=vacancies|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=International Marine Litter Research Unit team|url=https://www.plymouth.ac.uk/research/marine-litter/people|website=University of Plymouth}}</ref>

==Awards==
*2016: [[Marsh Award for Marine and Freshwater Conservation]] from the [[Zoological Society of London]] and [[Marsh Christian Trust]]<ref>{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=World leader in microplastic research receives award from the Zoological Society of London|url=https://www.plymouth.ac.uk/news/world-leader-in-microplastic-research-receives-award-from-the-zoological-society-of-london|website=University of Plymouth}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Marsh Christian Trust – Marsh Award for Marine and Freshwater Conservation|url=https://www.marshchristiantrust.org/award/marsh-award-for-marine-and-freshwater-conservation/|website=www.marshchristiantrust.org}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Prestigious awards honour the stars of conservation science|url=https://biaza.org.uk/news/detail/prestigious-awards-honour-the-stars-of-conservation-science|website=[[British and Irish Association of Zoos and Aquariums]]}}</ref>
*2018: [[Order of the British Empire]] (OBE) in the [[2018 New Year Honours]] for services to marine science<ref>{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Professor Richard Thompson made an OBE for services to marine science|url=https://www.plymouth.ac.uk/news/professor-richard-thompson-made-an-obe-for-services-to-marine-science|website=University of Plymouth}}</ref>

{{Short description|marine biologist}}
'''Richard C. Thompson''' [[Order of the British Empire|OBE]] is a [[Marine biology|marine biologist]] who researches [[Marine debris|marine litter]]. At the [[University of Plymouth]] he is director of the Marine Institute; professor of Marine Biology; and leads the International Marine Litter Research Unit. Thompson coined the term "[[Microplastics|microplastics]]" in 2004.<ref>{{cite news|first1=Stephen|last1=Buranyi|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=The missing 99%: why can't we find the vast majority of ocean plastic?|url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2019/dec/31/ocean-plastic-we-cant-see|newspaper=The Guardian|date=31 December 2019|issn=0261-3077|via=www.theguardian.com}}</ref>

==Career==
Thompson's paper, "Lost at Sea: Where is All the Plastic?",<ref>https://www.researchgate.net/publication/8575062_Lost_at_Sea_Where_Is_All_the_Plastic</ref> published in the journal ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'' in 2004, was the first to use the term [[microplastics]], which has since become common parlance.<ref>{{cite web|first1=Andrea|last1=Thompson|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Earth Has a Hidden Plastic Problem—Scientists Are Hunting It Down|url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/microplastics-earth-has-a-hidden-plastic-problem-mdash-scientists-are-hunting-it-down/|website=Scientific American}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=To Save the Oceans, Should You Give Up Glitter?|url=https://www.nationalgeographic.com/news/2017/11/glitter-plastics-ocean-pollution-environment-spd/|date=30 November 2017|website=National Geographic News}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Microplastic waste: This massive (tiny) threat to sea life is now in every ocean|url=http://www.independent.co.uk/news/science/microplastic-waste-this-massive-tiny-threat-to-sea-life-is-now-in-every-ocean-9602430.html|date=13 July 2014|website=The Independent}}</ref>

Since 2010 he has been professor of Marine Biology at the [[University of Plymouth]].<ref name="bio"/> Since 2018 he has also been director of the Marine Institute, part of the School of Biological and Marine Sciences at the University.<ref name="bio">{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Professor Richard Thompson OBE - University of Plymouth|url=https://www.plymouth.ac.uk/staff/richard-thompson|website=www.plymouth.ac.uk}}</ref> He also leads the University's International Marine Litter Research Unit.<ref>{{cite web|first1=University of Plymouth Drake Circus Plymouth Devon PL4 8AA United Kingdom +44 1752 600600|last1=Maps|first2=directions Visit us Job|last2=vacancies|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=International Marine Litter Research Unit team|url=https://www.plymouth.ac.uk/research/marine-litter/people|website=University of Plymouth}}</ref>

==Awards==
*2016: [[Marsh Award for Marine and Freshwater Conservation]] from the [[Zoological Society of London]] and [[Marsh Christian Trust]]<ref>{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=World leader in microplastic research receives award from the Zoological Society of London|url=https://www.plymouth.ac.uk/news/world-leader-in-microplastic-research-receives-award-from-the-zoological-society-of-london|website=University of Plymouth}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Marsh Christian Trust – Marsh Award for Marine and Freshwater Conservation|url=https://www.marshchristiantrust.org/award/marsh-award-for-marine-and-freshwater-conservation/|website=www.marshchristiantrust.org}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Prestigious awards honour the stars of conservation science|url=https://biaza.org.uk/news/detail/prestigious-awards-honour-the-stars-of-conservation-science|website=[[British and Irish Association of Zoos and Aquariums]]}}</ref>
*2018: [[Order of the British Empire]] (OBE) in the [[2018 New Year Honours]] for services to marine science<ref>{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Professor Richard Thompson made an OBE for services to marine science|url=https://www.plymouth.ac.uk/news/professor-richard-thompson-made-an-obe-for-services-to-marine-science|website=University of Plymouth}}</ref>

Thompson | birth_date = | birth_place = | death_date = | death_place = | death_cause = | resting_place = | resting_place_coordinates = | home_town = | other_names = | siglum = | pronounce = | citizenship = | nationality = | fields = [[Marine biology]]

[[University of Liverpool]] (PhD) | thesis_title = The Ecology of Epilithic Microalgae | thesis_url = https://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?uin=uk.bl.ethos.320574 | thesis_year = 1996 | doctoral_advisor = | academic_advisors = | doctoral_students = | notable_students = | known_for = | influences = | influenced = | awards = | spouse = | partner = | children = | signature = | signature_alt = | website = | footnotes = }} '''Richard Charles Thompson''' {{post-nominals|OBE|FRS}} is a [[Marine biology|marine biologist]] who researches [[Marine debris|marine litter]]. At the [[University of Plymouth]] he is director of the Marine Institute; professor of Marine Biology; and leads the International Marine Litter Research Unit. Thompson coined the term "[[microplastics]]" in 2004.{{cite news|first1=Stephen|last1=Buranyi|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=The missing 99%: why can't we find the vast majority of ocean plastic?|url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2019/dec/31/ocean-plastic-we-cant-see|newspaper=The Guardian|date=31 December 2019|issn=0261-3077|via=www.theguardian.com}}[https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/m000674n "Plastic pollution with Richard Thompson"] on ''The Life Scientific,'' BBC Radio 4 ==Education== Thompson was educated at [[Newcastle University|University of Newcastle]] and the [[University of Liverpool]] where he was awarded a Ph.D in 1996. ==Career and research== Thompson's paper, ''Lost at Sea: Where is All the Plastic?'',https://www.researchgate.net/publication/8575062_Lost_at_Sea_Where_Is_All_the_Plastic published in the journal ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'' in 2004, was the first to use the term [[microplastics]], which has since become common parlance.{{cite web|first1=Andrea|last1=Thompson|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Earth Has a Hidden Plastic Problem—Scientists Are Hunting It Down|url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/microplastics-earth-has-a-hidden-plastic-problem-mdash-scientists-are-hunting-it-down/|website=Scientific American}}{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=To Save the Oceans, Should You Give Up Glitter?|url=https://www.nationalgeographic.com/news/2017/11/glitter-plastics-ocean-pollution-environment-spd/|date=30 November 2017|website=National Geographic News}}{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Microplastic waste: This massive (tiny) threat to sea life is now in every ocean|url=http://www.independent.co.uk/news/science/microplastic-waste-this-massive-tiny-threat-to-sea-life-is-now-in-every-ocean-9602430.html|date=13 July 2014|website=The Independent}} Since 2010 he has been professor of Marine Biology at the [[University of Plymouth]]. Since 2018 he has also been director of the Marine Institute, part of the School of Biological and Marine Sciences at the University.{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Professor Richard Thompson OBE - University of Plymouth|url=https://www.plymouth.ac.uk/staff/richard-thompson|website=www.plymouth.ac.uk}} He also leads the University's International Marine Litter Research Unit.{{cite web|first1=University of Plymouth Drake Circus Plymouth Devon PL4 8AA United Kingdom +44 1752 600600|last1=Maps|first2=directions Visit us Job|last2=vacancies|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=International Marine Litter Research Unit team|url=https://www.plymouth.ac.uk/research/marine-litter/people|website=University of Plymouth}}{{Twitter}} ===Publications=== *Thompson, Richard. (2006). Plastics. In: ''Dominant Wave Theory.'' By Andrew Hughes. Pp. 112–116. London: Booth-Clibborn, 2006. {{ISBN|9781861542847}}. New York: Abrams, 2007. {{ISBN|9780810993099}}. *"[[Marine Strategy Framework Directive]]: TaskGroup 10 Report: Marine Litter." Luxembourg: [[Publications Office of the European Union]], 2010. Galgani, F., Fleet, D., van Franeker, J., Katsanevakis, S., Maes, T., Mouat, J.Oosterbaan, L., Poitou, I., Hanke, G., Thompson, R., Amato, E., Birkun A., and Janssen, C. {{ISBN|978-92-79-15653-3}}. *''[http://www.stapgef.org/sites/default/files/stap/wp-content/uploads/2013/05/Marine-Debris.pdf Marine Debris as a Global Environmental Problem: Introducing a solutions based framework focused on plastic: A STAP Information Document: November 2011].'' Washington, DC: [[Scientific and Technical Advisory Panel]], [[Global Environment Facility]], 2011. Richard C. Thompson, Bruce E. La Belle, Hindrik Bouwman, and Lev Neretin. Thompson was lead author. *''[https://www.cbd.int/doc/publications/cbd-ts-67-en.pdf Impacts of Marine Debris on Biodiversity: Current status and Potential Solutions].'' CBD Technical Series No. 67. Montreal: Secretariat of the [[Convention on Biological Diversity]]; Scientific and Technical Advisory Panel—GEF, 2012. {{ISBN|92-9225-444-8}}. Thompson was lead author. *Readman, J.W., DeLuna, F. Ebinhaus, R., Guzman, A.N., Price A.R.G., Readman, E.E. Sheppard, A.L.S., Sleight, A.S. Strum, R. Thompson, R.C. Tonkin, A.Wolschke, H., Wright, R., and Sheppard, R.C. (2013) ''Coral Reefs of the World.'' *Thompson, R.C. (2013) Plastics, Environment and Health. In: ''Accumulation: The Material Politics of Plastics.'' Edited by Gabrys, J., Hawkins, G. and Michael, M. Hardback: Routledge, 2013. {{ISBN|9780415625821}}. Paperback: Routledge, 2017. {{ISBN|9781138063068}}. Pp.150–169. ===Awards and honours=== *2016: Marsh Award for Marine and Freshwater Conservation from the [[Zoological Society of London]] and [[Marsh Christian Trust]]{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=World leader in microplastic research receives award from the Zoological Society of London|url=https://www.plymouth.ac.uk/news/world-leader-in-microplastic-research-receives-award-from-the-zoological-society-of-london|website=University of Plymouth}}{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Marsh Christian Trust – Marsh Award for Marine and Freshwater Conservation|url=https://www.marshchristiantrust.org/award/marsh-award-for-marine-and-freshwater-conservation/|website=www.marshchristiantrust.org}}{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Prestigious awards honour the stars of conservation science|url=https://biaza.org.uk/news/detail/prestigious-awards-honour-the-stars-of-conservation-science|website=[[British and Irish Association of Zoos and Aquariums]]}} *2018: [[Order of the British Empire]] (OBE) in the [[2018 New Year Honours]] for services to marine science{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Professor Richard Thompson made an OBE for services to marine science|url=https://www.plymouth.ac.uk/news/professor-richard-thompson-made-an-obe-for-services-to-marine-science|website=University of Plymouth}} * 2020: Elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS) {{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/Richard-Thompson-25317/|title=Richard Thompson|publisher=Royal Society|accessdate= 20 September 2020}} ==References== {{Reflist}} {{FRS 2020}} {{Authority control}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Thompson, Richard}} [[Category:Date of birth missing (living people)]] [[Category:Place of birth missing (living people)]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Alumni of Newcastle University]] [[Category:Marine biologists]] [[Category:Academics of the University of Plymouth]] [[Category:Fellows of the Royal Society]]

G. |last7=McGonigle |first7=Daniel |last8=Russell |first8=Andrea E. |journal=Science |volume=304 |issue=5672 |page=838 |pmid=15131299 |s2cid=3269482 }} published in the journal ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'' in 2004, was the first to use the term [[microplastics]], which has since become common parlance.{{cite web|first1=Andrea|last1=Thompson|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Earth Has a Hidden Plastic Problem—Scientists Are Hunting It Down|url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/microplastics-earth-has-a-hidden-plastic-problem-mdash-scientists-are-hunting-it-down/|website=Scientific American}}{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=To Save the Oceans, Should You Give Up Glitter?|url=https://www.nationalgeographic.com/news/2017/11/glitter-plastics-ocean-pollution-environment-spd/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190925011337/https://www.nationalgeographic.com/news/2017/11/glitter-plastics-ocean-pollution-environment-spd/|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 25, 2019|date=30 November 2017|website=National Geographic News}}{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Microplastic waste: This massive (tiny) threat to sea life is now in every ocean|url=http://www.independent.co.uk/news/science/microplastic-waste-this-massive-tiny-threat-to-sea-life-is-now-in-every-ocean-9602430.html|date=13 July 2014|website=The Independent}} Since 2010 he has been professor of Marine Biology at the [[University of Plymouth]]. Since 2018 he has also been director of the Marine Institute, part of the School of Biological and Marine Sciences at the University.{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Professor Richard Thompson OBE – University of Plymouth|url=https://www.plymouth.ac.uk/staff/richard-thompson|website=www.plymouth.ac.uk}} He also leads the University's International Marine Litter Research Unit.{{cite web|first1=University of Plymouth Drake Circus Plymouth Devon PL4 8AA United Kingdom +44 1752 600600|last1=Maps|first2=directions Visit us Job|last2=vacancies|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=International Marine Litter Research Unit team|url=https://www.plymouth.ac.uk/research/marine-litter/people|website=University of Plymouth}}{{Twitter}} He is a co-coordinator of [[The Scientists' Coalition for an Effective Plastics Treaty]],{{Cite web |title=Scientist About Us |url=https://ikhapp.org/scientist-about-us/ |access-date=2024-07-24 |website=Ikhapp |language=en}} and in September 2024 led a further study - also published in ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'' {{cite journal | url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.adl2746 | doi=10.1126/science.adl2746 | title=Twenty years of microplastic pollution research—what have we learned? | date=2024 | last1=Thompson | first1=Richard C. | last2=Courtene-Jones | first2=Winnie | last3=Boucher | first3=Julien | last4=Pahl | first4=Sabine | last5=Raubenheimer | first5=Karen | last6=Koelmans | first6=Albert A. | journal=Science | volume=386 | issue=6720 | bibcode=2024Sci...386L2746T | url-access=subscription }} - which stated that after two decades of research into [[microplastics]], the world had sufficient evidence to agree global action to tackle them. ===Publications === *Thompson, Richard. At the [[University of Plymouth]] he is director of the Marine Institute; professor of Marine Biology; and leads the International Marine Litter Research Unit. In 2025, ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' magazine listed him as one of [[Time 100|the world's 100 most influential people]].{{Cite web |date=2025-04-16 |title=Richard Thompson: The 100 Most Influential People of 2025 |url=https://time.com/collections/100-most-influential-people-2025/7273764/richard-thompson/ |access-date=2025-04-17 |website=TIME |language=en}} ==Education== Thompson was educated at [[Newcastle University|University of Newcastle]] and the [[University of Liverpool]], where he was awarded a PhD in 1996. ==Career and research== Thompson's paper, ''Lost at Sea: Where is All the Plastic?'',{{cite journal |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/8575062 |doi=10.1126/science.1094559|title=Lost at Sea: Where is All the Plastic? |year=2004 |last1=Thompson |first1=Richard C. |last2=Olsen |first2=Ylva |last3=Mitchell |first3=Richard P. |last4=Davis |first4=Anthony |last5=Rowland |first5=Steven J. |last6=John |first6=Anthony W. G. |last7=McGonigle |first7=Daniel |last8=Russell |first8=Andrea E. |journal=Science |volume=304 |issue=5672 |page=838 |pmid=15131299 |s2cid=3269482 }} published in the journal ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'' in 2004, has been reported to be the first to use the term [[microplastics]] in relation to plastic pollution, which has since become common parlance.{{cite web|first1=Andrea|last1=Thompson|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Earth Has a Hidden Plastic Problem—Scientists Are Hunting It Down|url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/microplastics-earth-has-a-hidden-plastic-problem-mdash-scientists-are-hunting-it-down/|website=Scientific American}}{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=To Save the Oceans, Should You Give Up Glitter?|url=https://www.nationalgeographic.com/news/2017/11/glitter-plastics-ocean-pollution-environment-spd/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190925011337/https://www.nationalgeographic.com/news/2017/11/glitter-plastics-ocean-pollution-environment-spd/|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 25, 2019|date=30 November 2017|website=National Geographic News}}{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Microplastic waste: This massive (tiny) threat to sea life is now in every there are examples of the term being used in relation to marine pollution dating back to the early 1990s,{{Cite journal |last=Ryan |first=Peter G. |date=1990 |title=Plastic and other artefacts on South African beaches: temporal trends in abundance and composition |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/283507743_plastic_and_other_artefacts_on_South_African_beaches_temporal_trends_in_abundance_and_composition |journal=South African Journal of Science |volume=86 |pages=450–452 |via=ResearchGate}} and there is evidence that the authors who first used the term had been exploring the topic for several years before.{{Cite journal |last=Ryan |journal=Marine Environmental Research |volume=23 |issue=3 |pages=175–206 |doi=10.1016/0141-1136(87)90028-6 |issn=0141-1136|url-access=subscription }}{{Cite journal |last=Ryan |first=Peter G |date=1988-01-01 |title=The characteristics and distribution of plastic particles at the sea-surface off the southwestern Cape Province, South Africa |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0141113688900153 |journal=Marine Environmental Research |volume=25 |issue=4 |pages=249–273 |doi=10.1016/0141-1136(88)90015-3 |issn=0141-1136|url-access=subscription }} Since 2010 he has been professor of Marine Biology at the [[University of Plymouth]]. Since 2018 he has also been director of the Marine Institute, part of the School of Biological and Marine Sciences at the university.{{cite web|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=Professor Richard Thompson OBE – University of Plymouth|url=https://www.plymouth.ac.uk/staff/richard-thompson|website=www.plymouth.ac.uk}} He also leads the university's International Marine Litter Research Unit.{{cite web|first1=University of Plymouth Drake Circus Plymouth Devon PL4 8AA United Kingdom +44 1752 600600|last1=Maps|first2=directions Visit us Job|last2=vacancies|accessdate=2020-01-02|title=International Marine Litter Research Unit team|url=https://www.plymouth.ac.uk/research/marine-litter/people|website=University of Plymouth}}{{Twitter}} He is a co-coordinator of [[The Scientists' Coalition for an Effective Plastics Treaty]],{{Cite web |title=Scientist About Us |url=https://ikhapp.org/scientist-about-us/ |access-date=2024-07-24 |website=Ikhapp |language=en}} and in September 2024 led a further study - also published in ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'' {{cite journal | url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.adl2746 | doi=10.1126/science.adl2746 | title=Twenty years of microplastic pollution research—what have we learned? | date=2024 | last1=Thompson | first1=Richard C. | last2=Courtene-Jones | first2=Winnie | last3=Boucher | first3=Julien | last4=Pahl | first4=Sabine | last5=Raubenheimer | first5=Karen | last6=Koelmans | first6=Albert A. | journal=Science | volume=386 | issue=6720 | bibcode=2024Sci...386L2746T | url-access=subscription }} - which stated that after two decades of research into [[microplastics]], the world had sufficient evidence to agree global action to tackle them. == Awards and honours == Thompson was named one of Time Magazine's 100 most influential people in 2025.{{Cite web |date=2025-04-16 |title=Richard Thompson: The 100 Most Influential People of 2025 |url=https://time.com/collections/100-most-influential-people-2025/7273764/richard-thompson/ |access-date=2026-07-02 |website=TIME |language=en}} He was awarded the 2023 [[Blue Planet Prize]] alongside Professor Tamara Galloway and Professor Penelope Lindeque,{{Cite web |last=Park |first=Plymouth Science |date=2023-06-19 |title=Plymouth researchers awarded 2023 Blue Planet Prize |url=https://www.plymouthsciencepark.com/plymouth-researchers-awarded-2023-blue-planet-prize/ |access-date=2026-07-02 |website=Plymouth Science Park |language=en-GB}} recognising groundbreaking work into global plastics pollution. He was elected as a Fellow of the Royal Society in 2020 for his scientific and policy contributions.{{Cite web |last=Ball |first=Jak |date=2020-05-04 |title=Plymouth's 'microplastics' professor gets prestigious honour |url=https://www.plymouthherald.co.uk/news/plymouths-microplastics-professor-gets-prestigious-4085233 |access-date=2026-07-02 |website=Plymouth Live |language=en}} In 2017, for services to marine science he received an [[Order of the British Empire|OBE (Officer of the Order of the British Empire)]].{{Cite web |title=Professor Richard Thompson OBE FRS {{!}} Royal Society Fellow |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/richard-thompson-25317/ |access-date=2026-07-02 |website=royalsociety.org |language=en}} == Selected works == *Thompson, Richard.
